Mutation of the catalytic Q61 disrupts coordination of a water molecule that is required for nucleophilic attack on the gamma phosphate of GTP, while G12 and G13 mutations abrogate interactions with RAS GAP proteins that are required for proper positioning of the Q61 residue (Trahey et al, 1987; Scheidig et al, 1999; Buhrman et al, 2010; Scheffzek et al,1997).
In addition to somatic mutations in cancer, RAS is also subject to germline mutations that lead to a group of developmental disorders collectively known as RASopathies (reviewed in Rauen, 2013; Tidyman and Rauen, 2009). Like their oncogenic counterparts, these RAS mutants show defective GTP hydrolysis and constitutive signaling (Schubbert et al, 2006; Schubbert et al, 2007).","className":"Summation","schemaClass":"Summation"}],"reviewStatus":{"dbId":9821382,"displayName":"five stars","definition":"externally reviewed","name":["five stars"],"className":"ReviewStatus","schemaClass":"ReviewStatus"},"isChimeric":false,"category":"transition","entityFunctionalStatus":[{"dbId":9651308,"displayName":"loss_of_function of RAS GAP mutants:GTP [plasma membrane]","className":"EntityFunctionalStatus","schemaClass":"EntityFunctionalStatus"}],"input":[{"dbId":9651282,"displayName":"RAS GAP mutants:GTP [plasma membrane]","stId":"R-HSA-9651282","stIdVersion":"R-HSA-9651282.1","maxDepth":3,"name":["RAS GAP mutants:GTP"],"speciesName":"Homo sapiens","crossReference":[12061074],"consumedByEvent":[9651280],"isChimeric":false,"species":[48887],"inDisease":true,"schemaClass":"Complex","className":"Complex"}],"normalReaction":{"dbId":5658435,"displayName":"RAS GAPs bind RAS:GTP","stId":"R-HSA-5658435","stIdVersion":"R-HSA-5658435.3","isInDisease":false,"isInferred":false,"maxDepth":1,"name":["RAS GAPs bind RAS:GTP"],"releaseDate":"2015-06-17","speciesName":"Homo sapiens","literatureReference":[5658433,5658404,208211,5658234],"species":[48887],"isChimeric":false,"category":"binding","className":"Reaction","diseaseReaction":[9651280],"schemaClass":"Reaction"},"className":"Reaction","schemaClass":"FailedReaction"}
